content.title: About
content.content: Ricotta is a soft, fresh cheese made from the whey of whole cow's milk. It has a delicate creamy flavor, a hint of sweetness, and a smooth, spreadable texture. Ricotta is used in desserts, pastas, casseroles, and as a stand‑alone snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “ricotta” comes from the Italian word meaning “re‑cooked.”
Traditionally ricotta is produced from the whey left over after making other cheeses such as Parmesan.
In Italy ricotta is often served drizzled with honey, nuts, or fresh berries.
Ricotta can be low‑fat or richer, depending on the fat content of the original milk.
In some regions ricotta is used as a filling for ravioli and cannelloni.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Ricotta provides a complete source of milk protein, important for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: These minerals support strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ricotta contains riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Fresh ricotta may contain live cultures that contribute to gut health.

items.title: Lower lactose content
items.content: Most of the lactose is removed with the whey, making ricotta easier to tolerate for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey should avoid ricotta.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Whole‑milk ricotta is relatively high in fat, so it should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Some ricotta varieties are salted; those watching sodium intake should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ricotta can be enjoyed on its own, mixed into fruit salads, spread on toast, used as a filling for pasta, casseroles, pizza, and incorporated into baked goods such as cheesecakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep ricotta in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Once opened, it is best used within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops a sour smell or visible mold.
